questions.questionTextEn: In an inner product space $V$, if $\|u\| = 3$, $\|v\| = 5$, and $\|u + v\| = 7$, then $\|u - v\|$ is equal to
questions.explanationEn: By the parallelogram law, $\|u + v\|^2 + \|u - v\|^2 = 2(\|u\|^2 + \|v\|^2)$. Substituting gives $49 + \|u - v\|^2 = 2(9 + 25) = 68$, so $\|u - v\|^2 = 19$ and $\|u - v\| = \sqrt{19}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM MA Topic • Vector Spaces & Linear Transformations (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following bilinear forms defines an inner product on $\mathbb{R}^2$ for $u = (u_1, u_2)$ and $v = (v_1, v_2)$?
optionsEn: $\langle u, v \rangle = u_1 v_1 - u_2 v_2$
$\langle u, v \rangle = u_1 v_1 + 3 u_1 v_2 + 3 u_2 v_1 + 4 u_2 v_2$
$\langle u, v \rangle = u_1 v_1 + 2 u_1 v_2 + 2 u_2 v_1 + 5 u_2 v_2$
$\langle u, v \rangle = 2 u_1 v_1 + u_1 v_2 - u_2 v_1 + 2 u_2 v_2$
questions.explanationEn: A bilinear form $\langle u, v \rangle = u^T A v$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$ is an inner product iff $A$ is symmetric and positive definite. For (C), $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 5 \end{pmatrix}$ is symmetric with leading principal minors $1 > 0$ and $\det(A) = 5 - 4 = 1 > 0$, so it is positive definite. For (A), $\langle (0,1),(0,1)\rangle = -1 < 0$; for (B), $\det\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\3&4\end{pmatrix} = -5 < 0$; for (D), $A$ is not symmetric.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM MA Topic • Vector Spaces & Linear Transformations (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Let $V = M_{2\times 3}(\mathbb{C})$ be the vector space of all $2 \times 3$ matrices with complex entries. What is the dimension of $V$ as a vector space over $\mathbb{R}$?
questions.explanationEn: As a complex vector space, $\dim_{\mathbb{C}} M_{2\times 3}(\mathbb{C}) = 2 \times 3 = 6$. Since $\dim_{\mathbb{R}}(\mathbb{C}) = 2$, the real dimension is $\dim_{\mathbb{R}} M_{2\times 3}(\mathbb{C}) = 2 \times 6 = 12$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM MA Topic • Vector Spaces & Linear Transformations (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Let $P_5(\mathbb{R})$ be the real vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $5$ with real coefficients. What is the dimension of the subspace $W = \{p \in P_5(\mathbb{R}) : p(0) = p'(0) = 0\}$?
questions.explanationEn: Write $p(x) = a_0 + a_1 x + a_2 x^2 + a_3 x^3 + a_4 x^4 + a_5 x^5 \in P_5(\mathbb{R})$. The conditions $p(0) = 0$ and $p'(0) = 0$ are equivalent to $a_0 = 0$ and $a_1 = 0$. Thus $W = \operatorname{span}\{x^2, x^3, x^4, x^5\}$, which has dimension $4$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM MA Topic • Vector Spaces & Linear Transformations (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Let $D : P_3(\mathbb{R}) \to P_3(\mathbb{R})$ be the differentiation operator $D(p) = p'$. What is the rank of $D$?
questions.explanationEn: Since $\dim P_3(\mathbb{R}) = 4$ and $\ker(C) = \{p \in P_3(\mathbb{R}) : p' = 0\} = \operatorname{span}\{1\}$ has dimension $1$, the Rank-Nullity Theorem gives $\operatorname{rank}(C) = 4 - 1 = 3$ (the image is $P_2(\mathbb{R})$).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM MA Topic • Vector Spaces & Linear Transformations (Set 01)
questions.topicTag: Vector Spaces over R and C
questions.questionTextEn: Consider the real vector space $W = \{A \in M_3(\mathbb{C}) : A^* = A \text{ and } \operatorname{tr}(A) = 0\}$, where $A^* = \overline{A}^T$. What is the dimension of $W$ over $\mathbb{R}$?
questions.explanationEn: The real vector space $H_3$ of all $3 \times 3$ Hermitian matrices has dimension $3^2 = 9$ over $\mathbb{R}$ ($3$ real diagonal entries and $3$ complex strictly upper-triangular entries). Since the trace of any Hermitian matrix is real, $\operatorname{tr} : H_3 \to \mathbb{R}$ is a surjective $\mathbb{R}$-linear functional, so $\dim_{\mathbb{R}}(W) = 9 - 1 = 8$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM MA Topic • Vector Spaces & Linear Transformations (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Let $A \in M_3(\mathbb{R})$ have $\operatorname{tr}(A) = 5$, and define the linear operator $L_A : M_3(\mathbb{R}) \to M_3(\mathbb{R})$ by $L_A(X) = AX$. What is the trace of the linear operator $L_A$?
questions.explanationEn: With respect to the column-ordered standard basis $\{E_{11}, E_{21}, E_{31}, E_{12}, E_{22}, E_{32}, E_{13}, E_{23}, E_{33}\}$ of $M_3(\mathbb{R})$, $L_A$ acts on each of the $3$ columns of $X$ identically via $A$. Thus the $9 \times 9$ matrix of $L_A$ is block-diagonal with three copies of $A$ on the diagonal, giving $\operatorname{tr}(L_A) = 3\operatorname{tr}(D) = 15$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM MA Topic • Vector Spaces & Linear Transformations (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Let $A \in M_3(\mathbb{R})$ be a fixed matrix of rank $2$. What is the dimension of the subspace $W = \{B \in M_3(\mathbb{R}) : AB = 0\}$?
questions.explanationEn: The condition $AB = 0$ holds if and only if each of the $3$ columns of $B$ belongs to $\ker(A)$. Since $\operatorname{rank}(A) = 2$, we have $\dim(\ker(A)) = 3 - 2 = 1$. As the $3$ columns of $B$ can be chosen independently from $\ker(A)$, $\dim(W) = 3 \times 1 = 3$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM MA Topic • Vector Spaces & Linear Transformations (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Equip $P_2(\mathbb{R})$ with the inner product $\langle f, g \rangle = \int_0^1 f(x)g(x)\,dx$. What is the orthogonal projection of $f(x) = x^2$ onto the subspace $P_1(\mathbb{R})$?
questions.explanationEn: An orthogonal basis of $P_1(\mathbb{R})$ is $\{u_0, u_1\}$ where $u_0(x) = 1$ and $u_1(x) = x - \frac{1}{2}$ (since $\int_0^1 (x - \frac{1}{2})\,dx = 0$). We have $\langle u_0, u_0 \rangle = 1$, $\langle u_1, u_1 \rangle = \frac{1}{12}$, $\langle x^2, u_0 \rangle = \frac{1}{3}$, and $\langle x^2, u_1 \rangle = \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{12}$. Thus the projection is $\frac{1/3}{1}(1) + \frac{1/12}{1/12}\left(x - \frac{1}{2}\right) = x - \frac{1}{6}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM MA Topic • Vector Spaces & Linear Transformations (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Let $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \in M_3(\mathbb{R})$. What is the dimension of the subspace $\operatorname{span}\{I_3, A, A^2, A^3, \dots\}$ of $M_3(\mathbb{R})$?
questions.explanationEn: Write $A = I_3 + E_{12}$, where $E_{12}^2 = 0$. Then $A^k = I_3 + k E_{12}$ for all integers $k \ge 0$. Thus every power $A^k$ lies in $\operatorname{span}\{I_3, E_{12}\}$, and since $I_3$ and $A$ are linearly independent, the span has dimension $2$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM MA Topic • Vector Spaces & Linear Transformations (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Let $S, T : V \to V$ be linear operators on a finite-dimensional real vector space $V$. Which of the following statements is/are ALWAYS TRUE?
optionsEn: If $S \circ T = I_V$, then $T \circ S = I_V$.
questions.explanationEn: (A) Since $V$ is finite-dimensional, $S \circ T = I_V$ implies $T$ is injective and hence invertible, so $S = T^{-1}$ and $T \circ S = I_V$; TRUE. (B) $\operatorname{im}(S + T) \subseteq \operatorname{im}(S) + \operatorname{im}(T)$, so $\operatorname{rank}(S + T) \le \operatorname{rank}(S) + \operatorname{rank}(T)$; TRUE. (C) FALSE: for $S = \begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}, T = \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, $ST = 0$ (rank $0$) while $TS = S$ (rank $1$). (D) FALSE: $S = I_V$ and $T = 2I_V$ have the same kernel and image but $S \neq T$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM MA Topic • Vector Spaces & Linear Transformations (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Let $T : P_2(\mathbb{R}) \to \mathbb{R}^2$ be the linear transformation defined by $T(p) = (p(0), p'(1))$. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: With respect to the standard bases $\{1, x, x^2\}$ and $\{(1,0), (0,1)\}$, the matrix of $T$ is $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$.
questions.explanationEn: We compute $T(1) = (1, 0)$, $T(x) = (0, 1)$, and $T(x^2) = (0, 2)$, giving the matrix $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$ ((A) TRUE). This matrix has rank $2$, so $T$ is surjective ((C) TRUE) and has nullity $3 - 2 = 1$ ((D) FALSE). Since $T(x^2 - 2x) = (0, 2 - 2) = (0, 0)$, $\ker(T) = \operatorname{span}\{x^2 - 2x\}$ ((B) TRUE).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM MA Topic • Vector Spaces & Linear Transformations (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Let $V = P_2(\mathbb{R})$ and define $f_0, f_1, f_2 \in V^*$ by $f_k(p) = p(k)$ for $k = 0, 1, 2$. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: $\{f_0, f_1, f_2\}$ is a basis of $V^*$.
The map $T : V \to \mathbb{R}^3$ given by $T(p) = (f_0(p), f_1(p), f_2(p))$ is an isomorphism.
Every linear functional $g \in V^*$ can be written uniquely as $g = c_0 f_0 + c_1 f_1 + c_2 f_2$ for some $c_0, c_1, c_2 \in \mathbb{R}$.
questions.explanationEn: A polynomial $p \in P_2(\mathbb{R})$ with $p(0) = p(1) = p(2) = 0$ has $3$ distinct roots and degree $\le 2$, so $p = 0$. Hence $T$ is injective, and since $\dim(V) = 3$, $T$ is an isomorphism ((B) TRUE). This implies $\{f_0, f_1, f_2\}$ is linearly independent and thus a basis of $V^*$ ((A) and (C) TRUE). Finally, Simpson's rule is exact on $P_2(\mathbb{R})$: checking on $1, x, x^2$ gives $\frac{1}{3}(1) + \frac{4}{3}(1) + \frac{1}{3}(1) = 2 = \int_0^2 1\,dx$, $\frac{1}{3}(0) + \frac{4}{3}(1) + \frac{1}{3}(2) = 2 = \int_0^2 x\,dx$, and $\frac{1}{3}(0) + \frac{4}{3}(1) + \frac{1}{3}(4) = \frac{8}{3} = \int_0^2 x^2\,dx$, so (D) is also TRUE.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM MA Topic • Vector Spaces & Linear Transformations (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In $\mathbb{R}^4$ with the standard inner product, if $\theta$ is the angle between $u = (1, 1, 1, 1)$ and $v = (1, -1, 1, 1)$, then $\cos\theta$ is equal to _________. (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: We have $\langle u, v \rangle = 1 - 1 + 1 + 1 = 2$ and $\|u\| = \|v\| = \sqrt{4} = 2$. Thus $\cos\theta = \frac{\langle u, v \rangle}{\|u\|\|v\|} = \frac{2}{2 \times 2} = 0.50$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM MA Topic • Vector Spaces & Linear Transformations (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In $\mathbb{R}^3$ with the standard inner product, the distance from the vector $(4, 1, 3)$ to the subspace $W = \{(x, y, z) \in \mathbb{R}^3 : x + 2y + 2z = 0\}$ is equal to _________.
questions.explanationEn: The unit normal vector to $W$ is $n = \frac{1}{3}(1, 2, 2)$. The distance from $v = (4, 1, 3)$ to $W$ is the length of its projection onto $W^\perp$, namely $|\langle v, n \rangle| = \frac{|4 + 2 + 6|}{3} = \frac{12}{3} = 4$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM MA Topic • Vector Spaces & Linear Transformations (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Let $T : P_3(\mathbb{R}) \to P_3(\mathbb{R})$ be defined by $T(p)(x) = p(2x)$. Then the trace of $T$ is equal to _________.
questions.explanationEn: With respect to the standard basis $\{1, x, x^2, x^3\}$, $T(x^k) = 2^k x^k$, so the matrix of $T$ is $\operatorname{diag}(1, 2, 4, 8)$. Its trace is $1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM MA Topic • Vector Spaces & Linear Transformations (Set 01)
questions.explanationEn: Since $u_2 = 2u_1$, we can factor $A = u_1 (v_1^T + 2v_2^T) = (1, 2, 3)^T (4, 1, 6)$. Because both $(1, 2, 3)^T$ and $(4, 1, 6)$ are nonzero, $A$ is a nonzero outer product and hence has rank $1$.

The first three columns form a $3 \times 3$ matrix with determinant $\det\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\1&-1&1\\1&2&3\end{pmatrix} = 1(-5) - 1(2) + 1(3) = -4 \neq 0$.
